By locating the memory physically closer to the CPU the time needed for the buses to settle is reduced, and by replacing the DRAM with SRAM, which hold the value in a form that does not require amplification to be read, the delay within the memory itself is eliminated.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System.fact: An authoritative server indicates its status of supplying definitive answers, deemed authoritative, by setting a protocol flag, called the "Authoritative Answer" (AA) bit in its responses.

Domain Name System.fact: This mechanism would place a large traffic burden on the root servers, if every resolution on the Internet required starting at the root. To improve efficiency, reduce DNS traffic across the Internet, and increase performance in end-user applications, the Domain Name System supports DNS cache servers which store DNS query result.

Domain Name System.fact: RFC 1912 conveys basic rules for determining appropriate TTL values, with 1 to 5 days as typical values, and 1 to 2 weeks for records such as addresses of mail hosts, or name servers which are not expected to change often.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System.fact: For example, assuming the IPv4 address 208.80.152.2 is assigned to Wikimedia, it is represented as a DNS name in reverse order: 2.152.80.208.in-addr.arpa. Domain Name System.fact: For example, assuming the IPv4 address 208.80.152.2 is assigned to Wikimedia, it is represented as a DNS name in reverse order: 2.152.80.208.in-addr.arpa. ARIN's servers delegate 152.80.208.in-addr.arpa to Wikimedia to which the resolver sends another query for 2.152.80.208.in-addr.arpa, which results in an authoritative response.

Domain Name System.fact: Alternatively, a single hostname may resolve to many IP addresses to facilitate fault tolerance and load distribution to multiple server instances across an enterprise or the global Internet.

Domain Name System.fact: Dynamic DNS (DDNS) updates a DNS server with a client IP address on-the-fly, for example, when moving between ISPs or mobile hot spots, or when the IP address changes administratively.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System.fact: The header section consists of the following fields: Identification, Flags, Number of questions, Number of answers, Number of authority resource records (RRs), and Number of additional RRs. The identification field is used to match responses with queries.

Domain Name System.fact: Transaction ID: 16 bits Transaction ID Flags: 16 bits The flag field consists of sub-fields as follows: QR: 1 bit Indicates if the message is a query (0) or a reply (1). AA: 1 bit Authoritative Answer, in a response, indicates if the DNS server is authoritative for the queried hostname.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: OPCODE: 4 bits The type can be QUERY (standard query, 0), _____ (inverse query, 1), or STATUS (server status request, 2)
Domain Name System.fact: OPCODE: 4 bits The type can be QUERY (standard query, 0), IQUERY (inverse query, 1), or STATUS (server status request, 2).

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: AA: 1 bit _____, in a response, indicates if the DNS server is authoritative for the queried hostname
Domain Name System.fact: AA: 1 bit Authoritative Answer, in a response, indicates if the DNS server is authoritative for the queried hostname.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: TC: 1 bit Trun_____, indicates that this message was truncated due to excessive length
Domain Name System.fact: TC: 1 bit TrunCation, indicates that this message was truncated due to excessive length.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: RD: 1 bit _____, indicates if the client means a recursive query
Domain Name System.fact: RD: 1 bit Recursion Desired, indicates if the client means a recursive query.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: RA: 1 bit _____, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server supports recursion
Domain Name System.fact: RA: 1 bit Recursion Available, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server supports recursion.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: AD: 1 bit _____, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server verified the data
Domain Name System.fact: AD: 1 bit Authentic Data, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server verified the data.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: CD: 1 bit _____, in a query, indicates that non-verified data is acceptable in a response
Domain Name System.fact: CD: 1 bit Checking Disabled, in a query, indicates that non-verified data is acceptable in a response.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System.question: RCODE: 4 bits _____ code, can be NOERROR (0), FORMERR (1, Format error), SERVFAIL (2), NXDOMAIN (3, Nonexistent domain), etc
Domain Name System.fact: RA: 1 bit Recursion Available, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server supports recursion. AD: 1 bit Authentic Data, in a response, indicates if the replying DNS server verified the data.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System.fact: Number of Questions: 16 bits Number of Questions.

Domain Name System.fact: Number of Additional RRs: 16 bits Number of Additional Resource Records.

Domain Name System.fact: Resource records of the same type are described as a resource record set (RRset), having no special ordering.

Domain Name System.fact: In addition, the classes Chaos (CH) and Hesiod (HS) exist.

Domain Name System.fact: RDATA is data of type-specific relevance, such as the IP address for address records, or the priority and hostname for MX records. Well known record types may use label compression in the RDATA field, but "unknown" record types must not (RFC 3597).

Domain Name System.fact: The AAAA record for a.x.example is needed to specify the mail exchanger IP address.

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System.fact: As a booting client may be assigned a different IP address each time from a DHCP server, it is not possible to provide static DNS assignments for such clients.

Domain Name System.fact: When the length of the answer exceeds 512 bytes and both client and server support Extension Mechanisms for DNS (EDNS), larger UDP packets may be used.

Domain Name System.fact: In 1989, RFC 1123 specified optional Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport for DNS queries, replies and, particularly, zone transfers.

Domain Name System.fact: ODoH combines ingress/egress separation (invented in ODNS) with DoH's HTTPS tunneling and TLS transport-layer encryption in a single protocol.

Domain Name System.fact: The privacy gains of Oblivious DNS can be garnered through the use of the preexisting Tor network of ingress and egress nodes, paired with the transport-layer encryption provided by TLS. Domain Name System.fact: ODoH combines ingress/egress separation (invented in ODNS) with DoH's HTTPS tunneling and TLS transport-layer encryption in a single protocol. The privacy gains of Oblivious DNS can be garnered through the use of the preexisting Tor network of ingress and egress nodes, paired with the transport-layer encryption provided by TLS.

Domain Name System.fact: In 1989, RFC 1123 specified optional Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) transport for DNS queries, replies and, particularly, zone transfers.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: The _____ was Suite of IETF specifications.
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) is a suite of extension specifications by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) for securing data exchanged in the Domain Name System (DNS) in Internet Protocol (IP) networks.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: As of _____, DNSSEC deployment is spotty
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: As of 2026, DNSSEC deployment is spotty.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: RFC 3833 of _____ documents some of the known threats to the DNS, and their solutions in DNSSEC
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: RFC 3833 of 2004 documents some of the known threats to the DNS, and their solutions in DNSSEC.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: All answers from _____ protected zones are digitally signed
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: The Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) attempt to add security, while maintaining backward compatibility. RFC 3833 of 2004 documents some of the known threats to the DNS, and their solutions in DNSSEC.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: Other standards (not _____) are used to secure bulk data (such as a DNS zone transfer) sent between DNS servers
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: While protecting IP addresses is the immediate concern for many users, DNSSEC can protect any data published in the DNS, including text records (TXT) and mail exchange records (MX), and can be used to bootstrap other security systems that publish references to cryptographic certificates stored in the DNS such as Certificate Records (CERT records, RFC 4398), SSH fingerprints (SSHFP, RFC 4255), IPsec public keys (IPSECKEY, RFC 4025), TLS Trust Anchors (TLSA, RFC 6698), or Encrypted Client Hello...

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: The _____ specifications (called DNSSEC-bis) describe the current DNSSEC protocol in great detail
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: Other standards (not DNSSEC) are used to secure bulk data (such as a DNS zone transfer) sent between DNS servers. DNSSEC cannot protect against false assumptions; it can only authenticate that the data is truly from or not available from the domain owner.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: With the publication of these new RFCs (March _____), an earlier RFC, RFC 2535 has become obsolete
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: With the publication of these new RFCs (March 2005), an earlier RFC, RFC 2535 has become obsolete.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: The full set of RFCs that specify _____ are collected in RFC 9364, which is also BCP 237
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: DNSSEC cannot protect against false assumptions; it can only authenticate that the data is truly from or not available from the domain owner. The DNSSEC specifications (called DNSSEC-bis) describe the current DNSSEC protocol in great detail.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: ICANN made DNSSEC mandatory for new generic top-level domains in 2014.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: The correct _____ record is authenticated via a chain of trust, starting with a set of verified public keys for the DNS root zone which is the trusted third party
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: The correct DNSKEY record is authenticated via a chain of trust, starting with a set of verified public keys for the DNS root zone which is the trusted third party. DNS resolvers verify the signature with a public key, stored in a DNSKEY record.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: DNS resolvers verify the signature with a public key, stored in a _____ record
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: The correct DNSKEY record is authenticated via a chain of trust, starting with a set of verified public keys for the DNS root zone which is the trusted third party. DNS resolvers verify the signature with a public key, stored in a DNSKEY record.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: To implement _____, several new DNS record types were created or adapted to use with DNSSEC: RRSIG (resource record signature) Contains the DNSSEC signature for a record set
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: To implement DNSSEC, several new DNS record types were created or adapted to use with DNSSEC: RRSIG (resource record signature) Contains the DNSSEC signature for a record set. DNSKEY Contains the public key that a DNS resolver uses to verify DNSSEC signatures in RRSIG records.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: DNSKEY _____ the public key that a DNS resolver uses to verify DNSSEC signatures in RRSIG records
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: To implement DNSSEC, several new DNS record types were created or adapted to use with DNSSEC: RRSIG (resource record signature) Contains the DNSSEC signature for a record set. DNSKEY Contains the public key that a DNS resolver uses to verify DNSSEC signatures in RRSIG records.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: DS (delegation signer) _____ the name of a delegated zone
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: DS (delegation signer) Holds the name of a delegated zone.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: NSEC (next secure record) _____ a link to the next record name in the zone and lists the record types that exist for the record's name
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: DNSKEY Contains the public key that a DNS resolver uses to verify DNSSEC signatures in RRSIG records. NSEC (next secure record) Contains a link to the next record name in the zone and lists the record types that exist for the record's name.

Domain Name System Security Extensions.subject: Computer & IT
Domain Name System Security Extensions.question: DNS resolvers use NSEC records to verify the non-existence of a record name and type as part of _____ validation
Domain Name System Security Extensions.fact: DNS resolvers use NSEC records to verify the non-existence of a record name and type as part of DNSSEC validation. These records can be used by resolvers to verify the non-existence of a record name and type as part of DNSSEC validation.

FIPS 140.fact: The Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) is operated jointly by the United States Government's National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Computer Security Division and the Communications Security Establishment (CSE) of the Government of Canada. The use of validated cryptographic modules is required by the United States Government for all unclassified uses of cryptography.

FIPS 140.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140.question: In addition to the specified levels, _____ 4.1.1 of the specification describes additional attacks that may require mitigation, such as differential power analysis
FIPS 140.fact: In addition to the specified levels, Section 4.1.1 of the specification describes additional attacks that may require mitigation, such as differential power analysis.

FIPS 140.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140.question: FIPS 140-2, issued on 25 May _____, takes account of changes in available technology and official standards since 1994, and of comments received from the vendor, tester, and user communities
FIPS 140.fact: FIPS 140-2, issued on 25 May 2001, takes account of changes in available technology and official standards since 1994, and of comments received from the vendor, tester, and user communities.

FIPS 140.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140.question: It was the main input document to the international standard ISO/IEC 19790:_____ Security requirements for cryptographic modules issued on 1 March 2006
FIPS 140.fact: It was the main input document to the international standard ISO/IEC 19790:2006 Security requirements for cryptographic modules issued on 1 March 2006.

FIPS 140.question: The draft issued on 11 Sep _____, however, reverted to four security levels and limits the security levels of software to levels 1 and 2
FIPS 140.fact: The draft issued on 11 Sep 2009, however, reverted to four security levels and limits the security levels of software to levels 1 and 2.

FIPS 140-2.fact: Basic security requirements are specified for a cryptographic module (e.g., at least one Approved algorithm or Approved security function shall be used).

FIPS 140-2.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-2.question: No specific physical security mechanisms are required in a _____ 1 cryptographic module beyond the basic requirement for production-grade components
FIPS 140-2.fact: No specific physical security mechanisms are required in a Security Level 1 cryptographic module beyond the basic requirement for production-grade components. An example of a Security Level 1 cryptographic module is a personal computer (PC) encryption board.

FIPS 140-2.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-2.question: An example of a _____ 1 cryptographic module is a personal computer (PC) encryption board
FIPS 140-2.fact: No specific physical security mechanisms are required in a Security Level 1 cryptographic module beyond the basic requirement for production-grade components. An example of a Security Level 1 cryptographic module is a personal computer (PC) encryption board.

FIPS 140-2.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-2.question: Physical security mechanisms required at _____ 3 are intended to have a high probability of detecting and responding to attempts at physical access, use or modification of the cryptographic module
FIPS 140-2.fact: No specific physical security mechanisms are required in a Security Level 1 cryptographic module beyond the basic requirement for production-grade components. An example of a Security Level 1 cryptographic module is a personal computer (PC) encryption board.

FIPS 140-2.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-2.question: NVLAP accredited _____ laboratories perform validation testing of cryptographic modules
FIPS 140-2.fact: NVLAP accredited Cryptographic Modules Testing laboratories perform validation testing of cryptographic modules.

FIPS 140-2.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-2.question: Cryptographic modules are tested against requirements found in _____ 140–2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules
FIPS 140-2.fact: Cryptographic modules are tested against requirements found in FIPS PUB 140–2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules.

FIPS 140-2.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-2.question: All of these lists are updated as new modules/implementations receive validation certificates from _____ and CSE
FIPS 140-2.fact: NIST maintains validation lists for all of its cryptographic standards testing programs (past and present). All of these lists are updated as new modules/implementations receive validation certificates from NIST and CSE.

FIPS 140-2.question: Its successor, FIPS 140-3, was approved on March 22, 2019, and became effective on _____ 22, 2019

FIPS 140-3.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-3.question: Initial publication was on March 22, _____ and it supersedes FIPS 140-2
FIPS 140-3.fact: Initial publication was on March 22, 2019 and it supersedes FIPS 140-2.

FIPS 140-3.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-3.question: The FIPS 140-3 (_____ Draft) was scheduled for signature by the Secretary of Commerce in August 2013, however that never happened and the draft was subsequently abandoned
FIPS 140-3.fact: The FIPS 140-3 (2013 Draft) was scheduled for signature by the Secretary of Commerce in August 2013, however that never happened and the draft was subsequently abandoned.

FIPS 140-3.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-3.question: The _____ draft of FIPS 140-3 was also abandoned, although the use of ISO/IEC 19790 did ultimately come to fruition
FIPS 140-3.fact: In 2014, NIST released a substantially different draft of FIPS 140-3, this version effectively directing the use of an International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC) standard, 19790:2012, as the replacement for FIPS 140-2. The 2014 draft of FIPS 140-3 was also abandoned, although the use of ISO/IEC 19790 did ultimately come to fruition.

FIPS 140-3.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-3.question: The reference to a _____-version of ISO/IEC 19790 was an inadvertent error in the Federal Registry posting, as 2012 is the most recent version
FIPS 140-3.fact: In 2014, NIST released a substantially different draft of FIPS 140-3, this version effectively directing the use of an International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC) standard, 19790:2012, as the replacement for FIPS 140-2. The 2014 draft of FIPS 140-3 was also abandoned, although the use of ISO/IEC 19790 did ultimately come to fruition.

FIPS 140-3.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-3.question: On August 12, _____, NIST formally released a statement on the Federal Register asking for comments on the potential use of portions of ISO/IEC 19790:2014 in the update of FIPS 140-2
FIPS 140-3.fact: On August 12, 2015, NIST formally released a statement on the Federal Register asking for comments on the potential use of portions of ISO/IEC 19790:2014 in the update of FIPS 140-2.

FIPS 140-3.subject: Computer & IT
FIPS 140-3.question: ISO/IEC 19790 has been reviewed and re-confirmed as recently as _____, but without changes, hence retaining the 2012 version nomenclature
FIPS 140-3.fact: ISO/IEC 19790 has been reviewed and re-confirmed as recently as 2018, but without changes, hence retaining the 2012 version nomenclature.

FIPS 140-3.question: FIPS 140-3 became effective on September 22, _____

FIPS 140-3.question: FIPS 140-2 testing was available until September 21, _____, creating an overlapping transition period of one year
FIPS 140-3.fact: FIPS 140-2 testing was available until September 21, 2021, creating an overlapping transition period of one year.

Fireplane.subject: Computer & IT
Fireplane.question: The _____ was Computer internal interconnect architecture.
Fireplane.fact: Fireplane is a computer internal interconnect created by Sun Microsystems. The Fireplane interconnect architecture is an evolutionary development of Sun's previous Ultra Port Architecture (UPA).

Fireplane.subject: Computer & IT
Fireplane.question: It was introduced in October _____ as the processor I/O interconnect in the Sun Blade 1000 workstation, followed in early 2001 by its use in the Sun Fire and Sun Fire 15K series enterprise servers
Fireplane.fact: It was introduced in October 2000 as the processor I/O interconnect in the Sun Blade 1000 workstation, followed in early 2001 by its use in the Sun Fire and Sun Fire 15K series enterprise servers.

Fireplane.subject: Computer & IT
Fireplane.question: Peak performance (in the Sun Blade _____) reached 67.2 GBytes/second or a sustained 9.6 Gbit/s (2.4 Gbit/s for each processor)
Fireplane.fact: It was introduced in October 2000 as the processor I/O interconnect in the Sun Blade 1000 workstation, followed in early 2001 by its use in the Sun Fire and Sun Fire 15K series enterprise servers. Fireplane.subject: Computer & IT
Fireplane.question: Overall peak bandwidth through the interconnect is 43 _____ per second
Fireplane.fact: Overall peak bandwidth through the interconnect is 43 Gbytes per second.

Fireplane.fact: Competing systems from makers such as SGI or the HP Superdome series use only a single level of coherency support and so require the more complex directory coherence to be used throughout.

Fireplane.subject: Computer & IT
Fireplane.question: They use an increased system clock by _____ to 150 MHz
Fireplane.fact: They use an increased system clock by 50% to 150 MHz.

Fireplane.subject: Computer & IT
Fireplane.question: Together these allow a snooping bandwidth of _____ addresses per second
Fireplane.fact: Together these allow a snooping bandwidth of 150 million addresses per second.

Firmware.subject: Computer & IT
Firmware.question: The _____ was Low-level computer software.
Firmware.fact: In computing, firmware (FW) is software that provides low-level control of computer hardware. For a relatively simple device, firmware may perform all control, monitoring and data manipulation functionality.

Firmware.subject: Computer & IT
Firmware.question: As of _____, modern vehicles also employ computer-controlled anti-lock braking systems (ABS) and computer-operated transmission control units (TCUs)
Firmware.fact: As of 2010, modern vehicles also employ computer-controlled anti-lock braking systems (ABS) and computer-operated transmission control units (TCUs).

Firmware.subject: Computer & IT
Firmware.question: Free software replacements for vendor flashing tools have been developed, such as _____
Firmware.fact: Free software replacements for vendor flashing tools have been developed, such as Flashrom.
